Starting from A' on BC, barycentrics of vertices of T' = A'B'C' can be expressed as functions of a real parameter t, as: * A' = 0 : 1-t : t * B' = (a^2-b^2+c^2)*t-a^2+b^2 : 0 : -(a^2-b^2+c^2)*t+c^2 * C' = -(a^2+b^2-c^2)*t+b^2 : (a^2+b^2-c^2)*t-a^2+c^2 : 0 and, for barycentrics of vertices of T" = A"B"C", let's take the parallel lines to the sidelines of T' through A, B, C. In this way, barycentrics of vertices of T" can be expressed as functions of the same parameter t, as: * A" = 1 : (t-1)*(-a^2+b^2+c^2)/((a^2-b^2+c^2)*t-a^2+b^2) : t*(-a^2+b^2+c^2)/((a^2+b^2-c^2)*t-b^2) * B" = ((a^2-b^2+c^2)*t-a^2+b^2)/(-a^2+b^2+c^2) : t-1 : ((a^2-b^2+c^2)*t-c^2)*(t-1)/((a^2+b^2-c^2)*t-a^2+c^2) * C" = ((a^2+b^2-c^2)*t-b^2)/(-a^2+b^2+c^2) : t*((a^2+b^2-c^2)*t-a^2+c^2)/((a^2-b^2+c^2)*t-c^2) : t *Now, let P=X(n) be a chosen ETC center of ABC and let P' = P-of-T' and P" = P-of-T".* Then: .LI0421 li{padding-bottom:10px; before.content:") ";} When t varies, P' moves on a line with tripole Q'(P), equivalent to: * Q'(P) = IsotomicConjugate(Anticomplement(IsotomicConjugate(PolarConjugate(Orthoassociate(P))))) * or, algebraically but simpler: * Q'(P) = BarycentricQuotient(AntigonalConjugate(P), P) * this is, for P = \(x : y : z\), normalized barycentrics: * Q'(P) = ((x+1)*x*SA+(y-1)*y*SB+(z-1)*z*SC) ^-1 : : When t varies, P" moves on a circle through X_4 and center O"(P) = reflection of P in X_5. As constructed, triangles T' and T" are homothetic for any t, and, as t varies, their homothetic center moves on the **Yff hyperbola** (see `Wolfram Mathworld's Yff Hyperbola <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/YffHyperbola.html>`__).
